start.README.md:
# Lanternfall

A small text-adventure engine: rooms, exits, items, a tiny parser. The engine is headless: a `Game` built from a world text, and `step(line)` which returns the exact reply text.

## World file

The world is text, one record per line; empty lines and lines starting with `#` are ignored; fields are separated by `|` and trimmed of surrounding spaces:

```
start <room id>
vault <room id>
room <id> | <title> | <description> [| dark]
exit <room id> <direction> <target room id> [<item id>]
item <id> | <room id or ~> | <name> | <aliases, comma separated> | <weight> | <points> | <examine text> [| light]
```

* Directions are `north south east west up down`. Exits are one-way: a world lists the way back separately. The order of the `exit` lines of a room is the order the exits are shown in.
* An exit with a fourth word is *locked*: it can only be used while the item with that id is in the inventory (the item is not consumed).
* An item lies in the room named by its second field (`~` = nowhere yet). Names and aliases are matched case-insensitively (store them in lower case). `light` items light up dark rooms.
* `weight` and `points` are integers. Items lie in a room in the order of the `item` lines, and an item that is dropped is appended to the room's list.
* All `room` lines come before the `exit` and `item` lines that mention them; ids are unique.

## The game

The hero starts in the `start` room with empty hands; that room counts as visited. There is no limit to what the hero can carry. `steps` counts the successful moves (`go` through an exit); `score` starts at 0. The first time the hero enters a room (the start room doesn't count) the score gains 1 point.

### Reading a command

`step(line)` takes a line and returns the reply text (no trailing newline, lines joined by `\n`). The line is lower-cased and split at whitespace; the words `the`, `a` and `an` are dropped. The first remaining word is the verb, the other words joined by single spaces are the *noun phrase* (possibly empty). Nothing left: `I don't understand.`

| words | meaning |
|---|---|
| `go`, `walk`, `move` | go in the direction named by the noun phrase |
| `look`, `l` | describe the room |
| `take`, `get`, `grab` | pick something up |
| `drop` | put something down |
| `inventory`, `inv`, `i` | list what is carried |
| `examine`, `x`, `inspect` | read an item's examine text |
| `score` | `Score: <score> in <steps> steps.` |
| a direction (`north`...) or its first letter (`n e s w u d`) as the verb, alone | same as `go <direction>` |

A direction word as the verb followed by more words, and any other verb, reply `I don't understand.` In a `go` command the noun phrase may be a direction word or its one-letter form.

### Replies

* **Describing a room** (also after moving into it): if the room is dark and no `light` item is in the inventory or lying in the room, the reply is `It is pitch dark.` Otherwise the lines `<title>`, `<description>`, `Exits: <directions in file order, joined by ", ">` (only if the room has exits) and `You see: <item names joined by ", ">.` (only if items lie here, in the room's order).
* **go**: a noun phrase that is not a direction: `Go where?`; no exit that way: `You can't go that way.`; a locked exit without its item: `The way is locked. You need the <item name>.` Otherwise the hero moves, `steps` grows, a first visit scores, and the reply is the description of the new room.
* **take**: no noun phrase: `Take what?`; dark room (as above): `It is too dark to see.`; `take all` in a room without items: `There is nothing to take.`, otherwise it tries every item of the room in the room's order and replies one line per item, `<item name>: <result>`; an item the hero already carries (matched by name or alias): `You already have the <item name>.`; no matching item in the room: `You can't see any <noun phrase> here.`; otherwise the item is taken: `Taken.`
* **drop**: no noun phrase: `Drop what?`; `drop all` with empty hands: `You are carrying nothing.`, otherwise one line per carried item in carrying order, `<item name>: <result>`; an item that is not carried: `You don't have any <noun phrase>.`; otherwise the item is put in the room (appended to the room's items): `Dropped.` If the room is the `vault`, the item has more than 0 points and it was never dropped in the vault before, the score gains the item's points and the reply is `Dropped. (+<points>)`.
* **inventory**: empty hands: `You are carrying nothing.`, otherwise `You are carrying: <names in carrying order, joined by ", ">.`
* **examine**: no noun phrase: `Examine what?`; dark room: `It is too dark to see.`; an item that is carried or lies in the room (carried items first, then the room's, first match wins): its examine text; otherwise `You can't see any <noun phrase> here.`

An item *matches* a noun phrase when the phrase equals its name or one of its aliases (all lower case). If several items match, the first in the order that is being searched wins.

## API (`lanternfall.py`)

```python
import lanternfall
g = lanternfall.Game(world_text)
g.step(line)     # the reply text
g.score()        # int
g.steps()        # int, successful moves
g.finished()     # bool, True once the turn limit ended the game
```

## Tests

`python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v` replays the scenario files in `tests/data/` (`tests/adapter.py` shows how the API is called; in a scenario command `\n` stands for a newline in the world text; the format is described at the top of `tests/test_scenarios.py`).

start.README.md:
# Lanternfall

A small text-adventure engine: rooms, exits, items, a tiny parser. The engine is headless: a `Game` built from a world text, and `step(line)` which returns the exact reply text.

## World file

The world is text, one record per line; empty lines and lines starting with `#` are ignored; fields are separated by `|` and trimmed of surrounding spaces:

```
start <room id>
vault <room id>
room <id> | <title> | <description> [| dark]
exit <room id> <direction> <target room id> [<item id>]
item <id> | <room id or ~> | <name> | <aliases, comma separated> | <weight> | <points> | <examine text> [| light]
```

* Directions are `north south east west up down`. Exits are one-way: a world lists the way back separately. The order of the `exit` lines of a room is the order the exits are shown in.
* An exit with a fourth word is *locked*: it can only be used while the item with that id is in the inventory (the item is not consumed).
* An item lies in the room named by its second field (`~` = nowhere yet). Names and aliases are matched case-insensitively (store them in lower case). `light` items light up dark rooms.
* `weight` and `points` are integers. Items lie in a room in the order of the `item` lines, and an item that is dropped is appended to the room's list.
* All `room` lines come before the `exit` and `item` lines that mention them; ids are unique.

## The game

The hero starts in the `start` room with empty hands; that room counts as visited. The hero can carry at most 5 weight units in total. `steps` counts the successful moves (`go` through an exit); `score` starts at 0. The first time the hero enters a room (the start room doesn't count) the score gains 1 point.

### Reading a command

`step(line)` takes a line and returns the reply text (no trailing newline, lines joined by `\n`). The line is lower-cased and split at whitespace; the words `the`, `a` and `an` are dropped. The first remaining word is the verb, the other words joined by single spaces are the *noun phrase* (possibly empty). Nothing left: `I don't understand.`

| words | meaning |
|---|---|
| `go`, `walk`, `move` | go in the direction named by the noun phrase |
| `look`, `l` | describe the room |
| `take`, `get`, `grab` | pick something up |
| `drop` | put something down |
| `inventory`, `inv`, `i` | list what is carried |
| `examine`, `x`, `inspect` | read an item's examine text |
| `score` | `Score: <score> in <steps> steps.` |
| a direction (`north`...) or its first letter (`n e s w u d`) as the verb, alone | same as `go <direction>` |

A direction word as the verb followed by more words, and any other verb, reply `I don't understand.` In a `go` command the noun phrase may be a direction word or its one-letter form.

### Replies

* **Describing a room** (also after moving into it): if the room is dark and no `light` item is in the inventory or lying in the room, the reply is `It is pitch dark.` Otherwise the lines `<title>`, `<description>`, `Exits: <directions in file order, joined by ", ">` (only if the room has exits) and `You see: <item names joined by ", ">.` (only if items lie here, in the room's order).
* **go**: a noun phrase that is not a direction: `Go where?`; no exit that way: `You can't go that way.`; a locked exit without its item: `The way is locked. You need the <item name>.` Otherwise the hero moves, `steps` grows, a first visit scores, and the reply is the description of the new room.
* **take**: no noun phrase: `Take what?`; dark room (as above): `It is too dark to see.`; `take all` in a room without items: `There is nothing to take.`, otherwise it tries every item of the room in the room's order and replies one line per item, `<item name>: <result>`; an item the hero already carries (matched by name or alias): `You already have the <item name>.`; no matching item in the room: `You can't see any <noun phrase> here.`; otherwise the item is taken: `Taken.` — unless the carried weight plus the item's weight would exceed 5: then `You can't carry that much.` and nothing moves.
* **drop**: no noun phrase: `Drop what?`; `drop all` with empty hands: `You are carrying nothing.`, otherwise one line per carried item in carrying order, `<item name>: <result>`; an item that is not carried: `You don't have any <noun phrase>.`; otherwise the item is put in the room (appended to the room's items): `Dropped.` If the room is the `vault`, the item has more than 0 points and it was never dropped in the vault before, the score gains the item's points and the reply is `Dropped. (+<points>)`.
* **inventory**: empty hands: `You are carrying nothing.`, otherwise `You are carrying: <names in carrying order, joined by ", ">.` followed by a second line `Weight <carried>/5.`
* **examine**: no noun phrase: `Examine what?`; dark room: `It is too dark to see.`; an item that is carried or lies in the room (carried items first, then the room's, first match wins): its examine text; otherwise `You can't see any <noun phrase> here.`

An item *matches* a noun phrase when the phrase equals its name or one of its aliases (all lower case). If several items match, the first in the order that is being searched wins.

## API (`lanternfall.py`)

```python
import lanternfall
g = lanternfall.Game(world_text)
g.step(line)     # the reply text
g.score()        # int
g.steps()        # int, successful moves
g.finished()     # bool, True once the turn limit ended the game
```

`python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v` replays the scenario files in `tests/data/` (`tests/adapter.py` shows how the API is called; in a scenario command `\n` stands for a newline in the world text; the format is described at the top of `tests/test_scenarios.py`).

start.README.md:
# Lanternfall

A small text-adventure engine: rooms, exits, items, a tiny parser. The engine is headless: a `Game` built from a world text, and `step(line)` which returns the exact reply text.

## World file

The world is text, one record per line; empty lines and lines starting with `#` are ignored; fields are separated by `|` and trimmed of surrounding spaces:

```
start <room id>
vault <room id>
room <id> | <title> | <description> [| dark]
exit <room id> <direction> <target room id> [<item id>]
item <id> | <room id or ~> | <name> | <aliases, comma separated> | <weight> | <points> | <examine text> [| light]
```

* Directions are `north south east west up down`. Exits are one-way: a world lists the way back separately. The order of the `exit` lines of a room is the order the exits are shown in.
* An exit with a fourth word is *locked*: it can only be used while the item with that id is in the inventory (the item is not consumed).
* An item lies in the room named by its second field (`~` = nowhere yet). Names and aliases are matched case-insensitively (store them in lower case). `light` items light up dark rooms.
* `weight` and `points` are integers. Items lie in a room in the order of the `item` lines, and an item that is dropped is appended to the room's list.
* All `room` lines come before the `exit` and `item` lines that mention them; ids are unique.

## The game

The hero starts in the `start` room with empty hands; that room counts as visited. There is no limit to what the hero can carry. `steps` counts the successful moves (`go` through an exit); `score` starts at 0. The first time the hero enters a room (the start room doesn't count) the score gains 0 points (that is: nothing).

### Reading a command

`step(line)` takes a line and returns the reply text (no trailing newline, lines joined by `\n`). The line is lower-cased and split at whitespace; the words `the`, `a` and `an` are dropped. The first remaining word is the verb, the other words joined by single spaces are the *noun phrase* (possibly empty). Nothing left: `I don't understand.`

| words | meaning |
|---|---|
| `go`, `walk`, `move` | go in the direction named by the noun phrase |
| `look`, `l` | describe the room |
| `take`, `get`, `grab` | pick something up |
| `drop` | put something down |
| `inventory`, `inv`, `i` | list what is carried |
| `examine`, `x`, `inspect` | read an item's examine text |
| `score` | `Score: <score> in <steps> steps.` |
| a direction (`north`...) or its first letter (`n e s w u d`) as the verb, alone | same as `go <direction>` |

A direction word as the verb followed by more words, and any other verb, reply `I don't understand.` In a `go` command the noun phrase may be a direction word or its one-letter form.

### Replies

* **Describing a room** (also after moving into it): if the room is dark and no `light` item is in the inventory or lying in the room, the reply is `It is pitch dark.` Otherwise the lines `<title>`, `<description>`, `Exits: <directions in file order, joined by ", ">` (only if the room has exits) and `You see: <item names joined by ", ">.` (only if items lie here, in the room's order).
* **go**: a noun phrase that is not a direction: `Go where?`; no exit that way: `You can't go that way.`; a locked exit without its item: `The way is locked. You need the <item name>.` Otherwise the hero moves, `steps` grows, a first visit scores, and the reply is the description of the new room. When `steps` reaches 12 the reply gets an extra last line `You have run out of time.` and the game is over: every later command (whatever it is) replies `The game is over.` and changes nothing.
* **take**: no noun phrase: `Take what?`; dark room (as above): `It is too dark to see.`; `take all` in a room without items: `There is nothing to take.`, otherwise it tries every item of the room in the room's order and replies one line per item, `<item name>: <result>`; an item the hero already carries (matched by name or alias): `You already have the <item name>.`; no matching item in the room: `You can't see any <noun phrase> here.`; otherwise the item is taken: `Taken.`
* **drop**: no noun phrase: `Drop what?`; `drop all` with empty hands: `You are carrying nothing.`, otherwise one line per carried item in carrying order, `<item name>: <result>`; an item that is not carried: `You don't have any <noun phrase>.`; otherwise the item is put in the room (appended to the room's items): `Dropped.` If the room is the `vault`, the item has more than 0 points and it was never dropped in the vault before, the score gains the item's points and the reply is `Dropped. (+<points>)`.
* **inventory**: empty hands: `You are carrying nothing.`, otherwise `You are carrying: <names in carrying order, joined by ", ">.`
* **examine**: no noun phrase: `Examine what?`; dark room: `It is too dark to see.`; an item that is carried or lies in the room (carried items first, then the room's, first match wins): its examine text; otherwise `You can't see any <noun phrase> here.`

An item *matches* a noun phrase when the phrase equals its name or one of its aliases (all lower case). If several items match, the first in the order that is being searched wins.

## API (`lanternfall.py`)

```python
import lanternfall
g = lanternfall.Game(world_text)
g.step(line)     # the reply text
g.score()        # int
g.steps()        # int, successful moves
g.finished()     # bool, True once the turn limit ended the game
```

## Tests

`python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v` replays the scenario files in `tests/data/` (`tests/adapter.py` shows how the API is called; in a scenario command `\n` stands for a newline in the world text; the format is described at the top of `tests/test_scenarios.py`).

start.README.md:
# Lanternfall

A small text-adventure engine: rooms, exits, items, a tiny parser. The engine is headless: a `Game` built from a world text, and `step(line)` which returns the exact reply text.

## World file

The world is text, one record per line; empty lines and lines starting with `#` are ignored; fields are separated by `|` and trimmed of surrounding spaces:

```
start <room id>
vault <room id>
room <id> | <title> | <description> [| dark]
exit <room id> <direction> <target room id> [<item id>]
item <id> | <room id or ~> | <name> | <aliases, comma separated> | <weight> | <points> | <examine text> [| light]
```

* Directions are `north south east west up down`. Exits are one-way: a world lists the way back separately. The order of the `exit` lines of a room is the order the exits are shown in.
* An exit with a fourth word is *locked*: it can only be used while the item with that id is in the inventory (the item is not consumed).
* An item lies in the room named by its second field (`~` = nowhere yet). Names and aliases are matched case-insensitively (store them in lower case). `light` items light up dark rooms.
* `weight` and `points` are integers. Items lie in a room in the order of the `item` lines, and an item that is dropped is appended to the room's list.
* All `room` lines come before the `exit` and `item` lines that mention them; ids are unique.

## The game

The hero starts in the `start` room with empty hands; that room counts as visited. The hero can carry at most 4 weight units in total. `steps` counts the successful moves (`go` through an exit); `score` starts at 0. The first time the hero enters a room (the start room doesn't count) the score gains 2 points.

### Reading a command

`step(line)` takes a line and returns the reply text (no trailing newline, lines joined by `\n`). The line is lower-cased and split at whitespace; the words `the`, `a` and `an` are dropped. The first remaining word is the verb, the other words joined by single spaces are the *noun phrase* (possibly empty). Nothing left: `I don't understand.`

| words | meaning |
|---|---|
| `go`, `walk`, `move` | go in the direction named by the noun phrase |
| `look`, `l` | describe the room |
| `take`, `get`, `grab` | pick something up |
| `drop` | put something down |
| `inventory`, `inv`, `i` | list what is carried |
| `examine`, `x`, `inspect` | read an item's examine text |
| `score` | `Score: <score> in <steps> steps.` |
| a direction (`north`...) or its first letter (`n e s w u d`) as the verb, alone | same as `go <direction>` |

A direction word as the verb followed by more words, and any other verb, reply `I don't understand.` In a `go` command the noun phrase may be a direction word or its one-letter form.

### Replies

* **Describing a room** (also after moving into it): if the room is dark and no `light` item is in the inventory or lying in the room, the reply is `It is pitch dark.` Otherwise the lines `<title>`, `<description>`, `Exits: <directions in file order, joined by ", ">` (only if the room has exits) and `You see: <item names joined by ", ">.` (only if items lie here, in the room's order).
* **go**: a noun phrase that is not a direction: `Go where?`; no exit that way: `You can't go that way.`; a locked exit without its item: `The way is locked. You need the <item name>.` Otherwise the hero moves, `steps` grows, a first visit scores, and the reply is the description of the new room.
* **take**: no noun phrase: `Take what?`; dark room (as above): `It is too dark to see.`; `take all` in a room without items: `There is nothing to take.`, otherwise it tries every item of the room in the room's order and replies one line per item, `<item name>: <result>`; an item the hero already carries (matched by name or alias): `You already have the <item name>.`; no matching item in the room: `You can't see any <noun phrase> here.`; otherwise the item is taken: `Taken.` — unless the carried weight plus the item's weight would exceed 4: then `You can't carry that much.` and nothing moves.
* **drop**: no noun phrase: `Drop what?`; `drop all` with empty hands: `You are carrying nothing.`, otherwise one line per carried item in carrying order, `<item name>: <result>`; an item that is not carried: `You don't have any <noun phrase>.`; otherwise the item is put in the room (appended to the room's items): `Dropped.` If the room is the `vault`, the item has more than 0 points and it was never dropped in the vault before, the score gains the item's points and the reply is `Dropped. (+<points>)`.
* **inventory**: empty hands: `You are carrying nothing.`, otherwise `You are carrying: <names in carrying order, joined by ", ">.` followed by a second line `Weight <carried>/4.`
* **examine**: no noun phrase: `Examine what?`; dark room: `It is too dark to see.`; an item that is carried or lies in the room (carried items first, then the room's, first match wins): its examine text; otherwise `You can't see any <noun phrase> here.`

An item *matches* a noun phrase when the phrase equals its name or one of its aliases (all lower case). If several items match, the first in the order that is being searched wins.

## API (`lanternfall.py`)

```python
import lanternfall
g = lanternfall.Game(world_text)
g.step(line)     # the reply text
g.score()        # int
g.steps()        # int, successful moves
g.finished()     # bool, True once the turn limit ended the game
```

## Tests

`python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v` replays the scenario files in `tests/data/` (`tests/adapter.py` shows how the API is called; in a scenario command `\n` stands for a newline in the world text; the format is described at the top of `tests/test_scenarios.py`).

start.README.md:
# Lanternfall

A small text-adventure engine: rooms, exits, items, a tiny parser. The engine is headless: a `Game` built from a world text, and `step(line)` which returns the exact reply text.

## World file

The world is text, one record per line; empty lines and lines starting with `#` are ignored; fields are separated by `|` and trimmed of surrounding spaces:

```
start <room id>
vault <room id>
room <id> | <title> | <description> [| dark]
exit <room id> <direction> <target room id> [<item id>]
item <id> | <room id or ~> | <name> | <aliases, comma separated> | <weight> | <points> | <examine text> [| light]
```

* Directions are `north south east west up down`. Exits are one-way: a world lists the way back separately. The order of the `exit` lines of a room is the order the exits are shown in.
* An exit with a fourth word is *locked*: it can only be used while the item with that id is in the inventory (the item is not consumed).
* An item lies in the room named by its second field (`~` = nowhere yet). Names and aliases are matched case-insensitively (store them in lower case). `light` items light up dark rooms.
* `weight` and `points` are integers. Items lie in a room in the order of the `item` lines, and an item that is dropped is appended to the room's list.
* All `room` lines come before the `exit` and `item` lines that mention them; ids are unique.

## The game

The hero starts in the `start` room with empty hands; that room counts as visited. The hero can carry at most 6 weight units in total. `steps` counts the successful moves (`go` through an exit); `score` starts at 0. The first time the hero enters a room (the start room doesn't count) the score gains 3 points.

### Reading a command

`step(line)` takes a line and returns the reply text (no trailing newline, lines joined by `\n`). The line is lower-cased and split at whitespace; the words `the`, `a` and `an` are dropped. The first remaining word is the verb, the other words joined by single spaces are the *noun phrase* (possibly empty). Nothing left: `I don't understand.`

| words | meaning |
|---|---|
| `go`, `walk`, `move` | go in the direction named by the noun phrase |
| `look`, `l` | describe the room |
| `take`, `get`, `grab` | pick something up |
| `drop` | put something down |
| `inventory`, `inv`, `i` | list what is carried |
| `examine`, `x`, `inspect` | read an item's examine text |
| `score` | `Score: <score> in <steps> steps.` |
| a direction (`north`...) or its first letter (`n e s w u d`) as the verb, alone | same as `go <direction>` |

A direction word as the verb followed by more words, and any other verb, reply `I don't understand.` In a `go` command the noun phrase may be a direction word or its one-letter form.

### Replies

* **Describing a room** (also after moving into it): if the room is dark and no `light` item is in the inventory or lying in the room, the reply is `It is pitch dark.` Otherwise the lines `<title>`, `<description>`, `Exits: <directions in file order, joined by ", ">` (only if the room has exits) and `You see: <item names joined by ", ">.` (only if items lie here, in the room's order).
* **go**: a noun phrase that is not a direction: `Go where?`; no exit that way: `You can't go that way.`; a locked exit without its item: `The way is locked. You need the <item name>.` Otherwise the hero moves, `steps` grows, a first visit scores, and the reply is the description of the new room. When `steps` reaches 20 the reply gets an extra last line `You have run out of time.` and the game is over: every later command (whatever it is) replies `The game is over.` and changes nothing.
* **take**: no noun phrase: `Take what?`; dark room (as above): `It is too dark to see.`; `take all` in a room without items: `There is nothing to take.`, otherwise it tries every item of the room in the room's order and replies one line per item, `<item name>: <result>`; an item the hero already carries (matched by name or alias): `You already have the <item name>.`; no matching item in the room: `You can't see any <noun phrase> here.`; otherwise the item is taken: `Taken.` — unless the carried weight plus the item's weight would exceed 6: then `You can't carry that much.` and nothing moves.
* **drop**: no noun phrase: `Drop what?`; `drop all` with empty hands: `You are carrying nothing.`, otherwise one line per carried item in carrying order, `<item name>: <result>`; an item that is not carried: `You don't have any <noun phrase>.`; otherwise the item is put in the room (appended to the room's items): `Dropped.` If the room is the `vault`, the item has more than 0 points and it was never dropped in the vault before, the score gains the item's points and the reply is `Dropped. (+<points>)`.
* **inventory**: empty hands: `You are carrying nothing.`, otherwise `You are carrying: <names in carrying order, joined by ", ">.` followed by a second line `Weight <carried>/6.`
* **examine**: no noun phrase: `Examine what?`; dark room: `It is too dark to see.`; an item that is carried or lies in the room (carried items first, then the room's, first match wins): its examine text; otherwise `You can't see any <noun phrase> here.`

An item *matches* a noun phrase when the phrase equals its name or one of its aliases (all lower case). If several items match, the first in the order that is being searched wins.

## API (`lanternfall.py`)

```python
import lanternfall
g = lanternfall.Game(world_text)
g.step(line)     # the reply text
g.score()        # int
g.steps()        # int, successful moves
g.finished()     # bool, True once the turn limit ended the game
```

## Tests

`python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v` replays the scenario files in `tests/data/` (`tests/adapter.py` shows how the API is called; in a scenario command `\n` stands for a newline in the world text; the format is described at the top of `tests/test_scenarios.py`).

start.README.md:
# Lanternfall

A small text-adventure engine: rooms, exits, items, a tiny parser. The engine is headless: a `Game` built from a world text, and `step(line)` which returns the exact reply text.

## World file

The world is text, one record per line; empty lines and lines starting with `#` are ignored; fields are separated by `|` and trimmed of surrounding spaces:

```
start <room id>
vault <room id>
room <id> | <title> | <description> [| dark]
exit <room id> <direction> <target room id> [<item id>]
item <id> | <room id or ~> | <name> | <aliases, comma separated> | <weight> | <points> | <examine text> [| light]
```

* Directions are `north south east west up down`. Exits are one-way: a world lists the way back separately. The order of the `exit` lines of a room is the order the exits are shown in.
* An exit with a fourth word is *locked*: it can only be used while the item with that id is in the inventory (the item is not consumed).
* An item lies in the room named by its second field (`~` = nowhere yet). Names and aliases are matched case-insensitively (store them in lower case). `light` items light up dark rooms.
* `weight` and `points` are integers. Items lie in a room in the order of the `item` lines, and an item that is dropped is appended to the room's list.
* All `room` lines come before the `exit` and `item` lines that mention them; ids are unique.

## The game

The hero starts in the `start` room with empty hands; that room counts as visited. There is no limit to what the hero can carry. `steps` counts the successful moves (`go` through an exit); `score` starts at 0. The first time the hero enters a room (the start room doesn't count) the score gains 1 point.

### Reading a command

`step(line)` takes a line and returns the reply text (no trailing newline, lines joined by `\n`). The line is lower-cased and split at whitespace; the words `the`, `a` and `an` are dropped. The first remaining word is the verb, the other words joined by single spaces are the *noun phrase* (possibly empty). Nothing left: `I don't understand.`

| words | meaning |
|---|---|
| `go`, `walk`, `move` | go in the direction named by the noun phrase |
| `look`, `l` | describe the room |
| `take`, `get`, `grab` | pick something up |
| `drop` | put something down |
| `inventory`, `inv`, `i` | list what is carried |
| `examine`, `x`, `inspect` | read an item's examine text |
| `score` | `Score: <score> in <steps> steps.` |
| a direction (`north`...) or its first letter (`n e s w u d`) as the verb, alone | same as `go <direction>` |

A direction word as the verb followed by more words, and any other verb, reply `I don't understand.` In a `go` command the noun phrase may be a direction word or its one-letter form.

### Replies

* **Describing a room** (also after moving into it): if the room is dark and no `light` item is in the inventory or lying in the room, the reply is `It is pitch dark.` Otherwise the lines `<title>`, `<description>`, `Exits: <directions in file order, joined by ", ">` (only if the room has exits) and `You see: <item names joined by ", ">.` (only if items lie here, in the room's order).
* **go**: a noun phrase that is not a direction: `Go where?`; no exit that way: `You can't go that way.`; a locked exit without its item: `The way is locked. You need the <item name>.` Otherwise the hero moves, `steps` grows, a first visit scores, and the reply is the description of the new room. When `steps` reaches 8 the reply gets an extra last line `You have run out of time.` and the game is over: every later command (whatever it is) replies `The game is over.` and changes nothing.
* **take**: no noun phrase: `Take what?`; dark room (as above): `It is too dark to see.`; `take all` in a room without items: `There is nothing to take.`, otherwise it tries every item of the room in the room's order and replies one line per item, `<item name>: <result>`; an item the hero already carries (matched by name or alias): `You already have the <item name>.`; no matching item in the room: `You can't see any <noun phrase> here.`; otherwise the item is taken: `Taken.`
* **drop**: no noun phrase: `Drop what?`; `drop all` with empty hands: `You are carrying nothing.`, otherwise one line per carried item in carrying order, `<item name>: <result>`; an item that is not carried: `You don't have any <noun phrase>.`; otherwise the item is put in the room (appended to the room's items): `Dropped.` If the room is the `vault`, the item has more than 0 points and it was never dropped in the vault before, the score gains the item's points and the reply is `Dropped. (+<points>)`.
* **inventory**: empty hands: `You are carrying nothing.`, otherwise `You are carrying: <names in carrying order, joined by ", ">.`
* **examine**: no noun phrase: `Examine what?`; dark room: `It is too dark to see.`; an item that is carried or lies in the room (carried items first, then the room's, first match wins): its examine text; otherwise `You can't see any <noun phrase> here.`

An item *matches* a noun phrase when the phrase equals its name or one of its aliases (all lower case). If several items match, the first in the order that is being searched wins.

## API (`lanternfall.py`)

```python
import lanternfall
g = lanternfall.Game(world_text)
g.step(line)     # the reply text
g.score()        # int
g.steps()        # int, successful moves
g.finished()     # bool, True once the turn limit ended the game
```

## Tests

`python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v` replays the scenario files in `tests/data/` (`tests/adapter.py` shows how the API is called; in a scenario command `\n` stands for a newline in the world text; the format is described at the top of `tests/test_scenarios.py`).

start.README.md:
# Lanternfall

A small text-adventure engine: rooms, exits, items, a tiny parser. The engine is headless: a `Game` built from a world text, and `step(line)` which returns the exact reply text.

## World file

The world is text, one record per line; empty lines and lines starting with `#` are ignored; fields are separated by `|` and trimmed of surrounding spaces:

```
start <room id>
vault <room id>
room <id> | <title> | <description> [| dark]
exit <room id> <direction> <target room id> [<item id>]
item <id> | <room id or ~> | <name> | <aliases, comma separated> | <weight> | <points> | <examine text> [| light]
```

* Directions are `north south east west up down`. Exits are one-way: a world lists the way back separately. The order of the `exit` lines of a room is the order the exits are shown in.
* An exit with a fourth word is *locked*: it can only be used while the item with that id is in the inventory (the item is not consumed).
* An item lies in the room named by its second field (`~` = nowhere yet). Names and aliases are matched case-insensitively (store them in lower case). `light` items light up dark rooms.
* `weight` and `points` are integers. Items lie in a room in the order of the `item` lines, and an item that is dropped is appended to the room's list.
* All `room` lines come before the `exit` and `item` lines that mention them; ids are unique.

## The game

The hero starts in the `start` room with empty hands; that room counts as visited. The hero can carry at most 3 weight units in total. `steps` counts the successful moves (`go` through an exit); `score` starts at 0. The first time the hero enters a room (the start room doesn't count) the score gains 1 point.

### Reading a command

`step(line)` takes a line and returns the reply text (no trailing newline, lines joined by `\n`). The line is lower-cased and split at whitespace; the words `the`, `a` and `an` are dropped. The first remaining word is the verb, the other words joined by single spaces are the *noun phrase* (possibly empty). Nothing left: `I don't understand.`

| words | meaning |
|---|---|
| `go`, `walk`, `move` | go in the direction named by the noun phrase |
| `look`, `l` | describe the room |
| `take`, `get`, `grab` | pick something up |
| `drop` | put something down |
| `inventory`, `inv`, `i` | list what is carried |
| `examine`, `x`, `inspect` | read an item's examine text |
| `score` | `Score: <score> in <steps> steps.` |
| a direction (`north`...) or its first letter (`n e s w u d`) as the verb, alone | same as `go <direction>` |

A direction word as the verb followed by more words, and any other verb, reply `I don't understand.` In a `go` command the noun phrase may be a direction word or its one-letter form.

### Replies

* **Describing a room** (also after moving into it): if the room is dark and no `light` item is in the inventory or lying in the room, the reply is `It is pitch dark.` Otherwise the lines `<title>`, `<description>`, `Exits: <directions in file order, joined by ", ">` (only if the room has exits) and `You see: <item names joined by ", ">.` (only if items lie here, in the room's order).
* **go**: a noun phrase that is not a direction: `Go where?`; no exit that way: `You can't go that way.`; a locked exit without its item: `The way is locked. You need the <item name>.` Otherwise the hero moves, `steps` grows, a first visit scores, and the reply is the description of the new room. When `steps` reaches 30 the reply gets an extra last line `You have run out of time.` and the game is over: every later command (whatever it is) replies `The game is over.` and changes nothing.
* **take**: no noun phrase: `Take what?`; dark room (as above): `It is too dark to see.`; `take all` in a room without items: `There is nothing to take.`, otherwise it tries every item of the room in the room's order and replies one line per item, `<item name>: <result>`; an item the hero already carries (matched by name or alias): `You already have the <item name>.`; no matching item in the room: `You can't see any <noun phrase> here.`; otherwise the item is taken: `Taken.` — unless the carried weight plus the item's weight would exceed 3: then `You can't carry that much.` and nothing moves.
* **drop**: no noun phrase: `Drop what?`; `drop all` with empty hands: `You are carrying nothing.`, otherwise one line per carried item in carrying order, `<item name>: <result>`; an item that is not carried: `You don't have any <noun phrase>.`; otherwise the item is put in the room (appended to the room's items): `Dropped.` If the room is the `vault`, the item has more than 0 points and it was never dropped in the vault before, the score gains the item's points and the reply is `Dropped. (+<points>)`.
* **inventory**: empty hands: `You are carrying nothing.`, otherwise `You are carrying: <names in carrying order, joined by ", ">.` followed by a second line `Weight <carried>/3.`
* **examine**: no noun phrase: `Examine what?`; dark room: `It is too dark to see.`; an item that is carried or lies in the room (carried items first, then the room's, first match wins): its examine text; otherwise `You can't see any <noun phrase> here.`

An item *matches* a noun phrase when the phrase equals its name or one of its aliases (all lower case). If several items match, the first in the order that is being searched wins.

## API (`lanternfall.py`)

```python
import lanternfall
g = lanternfall.Game(world_text)
g.step(line)     # the reply text
g.score()        # int
g.steps()        # int, successful moves
g.finished()     # bool, True once the turn limit ended the game
```

`python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v` replays the scenario files in `tests/data/` (`tests/adapter.py` shows how the API is called; in a scenario command `\n` stands for a newline in the world text; the format is described at the top of `tests/test_scenarios.py`).
